newsitem.title: FRANCE: Milosevic admitted losing local polls - Bulatovic.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic admitted losing local polls - Bulatovic.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic admitted shortly after November local elections that the opposition had won in Nis and Belgrade, Montenegro President Momir Bulatovic said in an interview published on Friday.
"Stealing votes cannot occur without consequences," Bulatovic told the French daily Le Figaro.
"It is natural that fixing an election would trigger demonstrations," the Montenegro leader said.

Bulatovic said he had asked Milosevic on November 21, a few days after the local poll, whether the loss of Belgrade and Nis would be a big problem for the Serbian leader. Serbia and Montenegro together make up the Yugoslav republic.
"He told me, "No, on the contrary, that will encourage the party to work harder to prepare for the next elections," Bulatovic said.

He said he was concerned by the wave of protests in Belgrade over the election aftermath, "because this has become a serious obstacle to the Yugoslav republic's reintegration into the world community".

Opposition Zajedno supporters and students have staged 33 days of demonstrations over alleged vote-rigging which overturned opposition victories in 15 of Serbia's biggest towns, including the capital.

The protests "are legitimate," he went on. "The opposition and the students have the absolute right to express their opinions. I am sorry that the authorities and the opposition did not found a way to settle this crisis from the very start".
He said differences in neighbouring Montenegro were settled by debate in the parliament, broadcast live to the public on television.
"Serbia should do the same thing," he said, saying he had personally asked Milosevic to resolve the crisis as soon as possible.
"Unfortunately, that is all I can do," he said, noting that Serbia is governed independently.

A delegation from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), arrived in Belgrade on Friday to investigate the election fraud allegations, and Bulatovic said he hoped the OSCE experts could now resolve the matter.
